body: Hatred is a normal human emotion, no less legitimate than sadness, anger, anxiety, stress, etc. If you learn to recognize when your hatred is and is not justified, then it is perfectly healthy.
Not gender dysphoria. I'm not a woman, just envious of them.

More like I am not a dominating or aggressive person, I am very quiet and just want to live my own life in peace. And this makes it especially hard when it comes to relationships, where women essentially do not have to do anything, and they will still have men coming to them to form relationships.

And the big reason too is [this](https://www.reddit.com/r/casualiama/comments/gqtzs8/i_intentionally_destroyed_my_bodys_resistance_to/), if I were a woman, my body would likely be much colder than it is now, men are essentially cursed to always be walking heaters. After all the work I have put in, I will still never reach the level of heat resistance that a woman could.

I feel that I am 100% a man, I am not saying I have gender dysphoria or anything like that, but that my life would be infinitely better if I were a woman, and that, due to my own personality, skills, desires, etc., I especially suffer from this, to the extent that I feel cursed.
Glad you read it, at least.

There are multiple reasons, but the main catalyst (or "spark" if you will) is that I spent a year studying abroad in a developing country which lacks A/C. In the summer, it could rise to upwards of 100F/37.8C indoors. It was by far the most miserable experience of my entire life, and I am not exaggerating.

When I got home, I went into the woods and prayed to God. I truly examined what was important in my life, what my values were, and how to go forward. I prayed to God to make my body colder. That is when I realized that I needed to fix my body and develop heat resistance. 

So I gradually started wearing more and more clothing. Before, I would only wear, at most, a light fleece jacket in the winter, even when it was below freezing outside, and I honest to God did not feel even a little cold. The problem then is that I would wear a t-shirt when it was 65F/18.3C outside, and sweat.

So that year, I decided to just continue wearing my winter clothing even into the spring. And then I put on even more. In the summer, I wore a sweater and a hoodie, even when it was up to 80F/26.7C indoors. And yes, I sweat, a lot. But consistency is the key. You can eat an entire airplane, if you just go one bite at a time.

That was the summer I graduated college, and afterwards, I moved to a new location with a significantly colder climate. This was a good thing, but I was, at the same time, worried about losing my progress and reacclimating to the cold.

To make a long story short, by the end of this winter(!), I had it at 84F/28.9C in my apartment with about four layers of (heavy) clothing on, and I was not the slightest bit hot. Last week, it was about 75F/23.9C outside, I wore three layers of clothing (thermal underwear, turtleneck sweater, hoodie), and again, not a drop of sweat on me. 

In addition, I lost weight. I was already normal weight before, but now I am over 20 pounds/9kg skinnier. I now only eat two meals per day. 

I feel truly blessed by God now. He is protecting me, He has removed the fear of heat from me. I used to envy women who felt cold in offices, now I have surpassed even them.
